099:1: In a fast-changing society, how can religion lead the world by changing people, without being bound to institutions?
099:4: In Paper 98 we saw the path the Melchizedek teachings took in the West through philosophy, cults, and the church. Now Paper 99 turns from history to the present and asks what relationship religion should have with society. The book says that religion achieves its highest social ministry when it has the least association with the secular institutions of society (99:0.1).
099:5: In the past, religion worked to turn evil into good within the existing social order, and so it indirectly sided with keeping that order. But religion should not directly take part in creating new social orders or in preserving old ones. True religion opposes violence, but it does not oppose society’s intellectual efforts to adjust its institutions to new conditions (99:0.1-0.2). As living conditions changed rapidly in the twentieth century, religion too was called upon to adapt quickly (99:0.3).
099:6: So in a society that never stops changing, what must religion hold on to, and what must it let go?

The ship of society has left the safe harbor of tradition and set out on the open sea. In this dangerous time of transition, religion’s most important social mission is to stabilize the ideals of mankind (99:1.3).
099:13: Religion has no new duties. But it is urgently called upon to act as a wise guide and experienced counselor (99:1.4). Humanitarianism without God is noble, but only true religion can make one group respond lastingly to the sufferings of another (99:1.5). Religion does not plunge directly into the secular work of social reconstruction, but it must keep restating its moral mandates and spiritual precepts in new language (99:1.6).

Only the true religion of personal spiritual experience can work creatively in this crisis.
099:19: That is why religionists must act in society and politics as individuals, not as groups. The moment a religious group acts collectively outside religion, it becomes a political party or an economic organization (99:2.3). The church’s only proper attitude is to teach peaceful evolution in place of violent revolution (99:2.5). The religion of living experience moves ahead of social change and becomes a moral stabilizer and spiritual guide (99:2.6).

103:1: Though each person believes differently and theology can be wrong, how can religious experience still be genuine and valid?

104:1: How did man’s habit of thinking in threes grow into an understanding of the Trinity of the one God and the seven triunities of infinity?
104:4: In Paper 103 we looked at the reality of religious experience. 105:1: From the I AM, without beginning or end, how did our finite universe and time come into being?
105:4: In Paper 104 we saw how the Father holds infinity together as one through the Trinity and the seven triunities. Now Paper 105 goes back still further and takes up the mystery of eternity: the origin and destiny of all that is called real (105:0.1).
105:5: Even to the high intelligences of the universe, infinity can be understood only in part. The totality of reality is infinity, and no mind less than infinite can fully comprehend it (105:0.1-0.2). So the presenter first admits that this explanation must suffer serious distortion as it is brought down to the level of mortal understanding (105:0.3). As one way of understanding infinity, we are invited to imagine a vast ellipse that comes from one absolute cause, diversifies without end, and seeks an infinite destiny (105:0.1).
105:6: So where did all reality come from, and how could a finite world with beginnings and growth—and we ourselves—come forth from the Infinite One?
105:8: The face which the Infinite turns toward all universe personalities is the face of a Father, the Universal Father of love. (105:1.8)
105:12: The philosophers of the universe attribute the absolute primal causation in infinity to the Universal Father functioning as the I AM. This concept is so far from human experience that it easily leads to misunderstanding, yet it gives a basis for a partial grasp of absolute origins and infinite destinies (105:1.1-1.2). The I AM is neither deified nor undeified, neither personal nor impersonal. No limitation can be placed on him except the fact that he exists (105:1.4).
105:13: Here an important distinction appears. The Father we know is that phase of the Infinite we perceive as experiential reality in our personality, while the I AM is a hypothesis covering everything we feel we cannot know (105:1.6). Even the master universe we stand in awe of may be only a partial revelation of the Infinite (105:1.7). But our concept of infinity will keep growing throughout eternity (105:1.8).

105:20: A philosophic hypothesis about all that cannot be known
105:23: All absolute realities—the three persons of Deity, the Isle of Paradise, and the three Absolutes—are from eternity and have no beginning. We put them in order in the language of time only to explain them to humans (105:2.1). In this explanation the I AM is pictured first as solitary, then as triune, and finally as sevenfold in seven phases (105:2.2-2.4).

105:30: Cause of Paradise — God as pattern
105:32: One with the Son — conjoint personality and the appearance of Havona
105:40: The I AM as I AM — the self-relationship of all things
105:42: The first phase can be partly experienced on the spiritual level, through worship, even by mortals in the flesh (105:2.5). And divine creativity is always characterized by unity, because it is the outward reflection of the oneness of the Father-Son and of the Trinity (105:2.7). In the seventh phase all of us, from the creatures of space to the citizens of Paradise, live and move and have our being (105:2.11).
105:44: The seven primal relationships within the I AM are eternalized as the Seven Absolutes of Infinity. We describe them in sequence, but in reality all seven Absolutes are without beginning, co-ordinately eternal, and the premises of reality (105:3.1).

105:53: The Isle of Paradise — the absolute of patterns, controller of gravity

105:59: The sum of undeified reality, the boundless quiet
105:61: The unifier of the deified and the undeified
105:63: All seven Absolutes taken together equal infinity, but the Universal Father himself is actually infinite (105:3.2). Paradise is not in space; rather, space exists relative to Paradise (105:3.4). The relationships of the Absolutes are hard to express in the language of time without paradox, but it is fact and truth that all reality rests on their eternal existence and relationships (105:3.10).
105:65: The self-revelation of the I AM moves from the static self, through self-segmentation and self-relationship, to relationship with the Absolutes that came forth from himself (105:4.2). It is often said that unity begets duality, duality begets triunity, and triunity is the ancestor of all things (105:4.3).

105:74: Between the sevenfold I AM and the Seven Absolutes
105:77: The functional association of the Seven Absolutes
105:80: The pre-existential becomes existential in the Seven Absolutes, and the existential becomes functional in the triunities. In this way the stage of the universe is set, and the diversification of energy, the diffusion of spirit, and the bestowal of personality and mind follow (105:4.8-4.9).
105:82: Finite reality was promulgated by the volitional act of the Paradise Deities and the adjustments of the triunities (105:5.1). The possibility of the finite lay in the infinite, but it was the Father’s free will that made it actual. Only the infinity of the Father’s will could qualify the absolute level so as to create the finite (105:5.4).
105:83: With this began the cycle of growth that comes down from the heights of infinity to the finite and then swings inward again toward Paradise, and with it began universe history and time itself (105:5.5-5.6). The new finite reality exists in two original phases, and from the relations between them a third type appears (105:5.7-5.10).

105:93: Creatures and creations of the superuniverse type
105:95: Neither perfect nor perfected, yet co-ordinate with both
105:96: Things, meanings, and values arising from relations of the two types
105:98: The perfect and the perfected are co-ordinate in eternity, but in time they appear different, because whatever is growing must appear incomplete in time (105:5.9).
105:100: When finite reality was promulgated, a number of repercussions followed (105:6.1). Among them, the creature repercussion gives this paper’s most practical insight. Attaining perfection by evolution implies a starting point that is not perfect, and from this comes incompleteness. This is the origin of potential evil; disharmony and conflict are inherent in evolutionary growth (105:6.4).

105:107: Activation of the architectural plan of the seven superuniverses
105:109: The appearance of Havona natives and evolutionary ascenders; the origin of potential evil

105:116: The time lag of evolution produces incompleteness, but at the same time it gives creatures the opportunity to take part in creation as partners with Deity. Even the material mind of the mortal becomes a partner with the divine Adjuster in building the immortal soul (105:6.5).
105:118: Transcendentals are realities that fall short of the infinite and the absolute but go beyond the finite and the creature. They appear as an integrating level linking the supervalues of the absolute with the maximum values of the finite (105:7.1). Havona is a good illustration. It is eternal yet not without growth, neither absolute nor finite, and it serves as a buffer between Paradise and the finite creation. But Havona itself is not a transcendental—it is Havona (105:7.2).
105:125: The Ultimate — different not only in degree but also in quality

105:139: Certain values of spirit; certain meanings of mind

105:143: All these realities are unified absolutely by the triunities, functionally by the Architects of the Master Universe, and relatively by the Seven Master Spirits (105:7.16). And the diversification of the First Source and Center may continue outward from age to age, proceeding on into the vastness of absolute infinity (105:7.18).
105:145: Paper 105 takes us to the farthest place the human mind can reach. The I AM, who has no beginning, reveals himself in seven phases; those relationships are eternalized as the Seven Absolutes; and through the triunities, the associations of the Absolutes, the stage of the universe is set. Then, because the Father’s free will qualified the absolute, time and the finite world came into being. Incompleteness and conflict come with that road of growth, but thanks to that very time lag we take part in creation as partners with Deity. Though infinity can never be fully fathomed, the face the Infinite turns toward us is always the face of a loving Father.

106:1: Where do we, as incomplete finites, stand among the many levels of reality, and where does that endless ladder lead?
106:4: In Paper 105 we saw how the Seven Absolutes and the finite world came forth from the I AM. Now Paper 106 takes up the opposite direction: how divided realities are integrated into oneness again. For the ascending mortal must understand not only the relation of Deity to reality, but also his own relation to the various realities (106:0.1).
106:5: This paper groups reality into seven levels. We mortals of Urantia are at the very bottom—the level of incomplete finites (106:0.3). The presenter first explains, however, that these divisions are symbolic compromise concepts, bound by mortal language and mind, the limited development of the superuniverses, and so on, and are wholly relative (106:0.10-0.17). And he says that reality grows in every universe age, with fullness forever being superimposed upon completion (106:0.18).
106:6: So how far does this growth, which begins with incomplete beings like us, reach beyond the Supreme Being and the Ultimate, and what will we meet at the end of that whole journey?
106:8: The quest for God is endless! (106:7.5)
106:16: The present status of ascending creatures — Urantia mortals
106:18: Experiential creatures who have attained the destiny of the present age
106:20: Implies prefinite origins and postfinite significance
106:22: That which is of master universe significance
106:24: Projected upon a supermaster universe field of creative expression
106:26: The eternity presence of the seven existential Absolutes
106:28: Reality before all beginnings and after all destinies
106:30: The primary phase of finite reality appears at once as the perfect personalities and perfect creation of Havona. But the secondary phase, bound by time and matter, is integrated only through growth and attainment (106:1.1). Because of this time lag, creatures can enter into partnership with the Creator in their own evolution (106:1.2).
106:31: During those ages of growth, God the Sevenfold links the incomplete with the perfect. However far a place may be from Paradise, God the Sevenfold extends his ministry of truth, beauty, and goodness to the struggling creatures there (106:1.3). Sevenfold Deity is at present the source of the relative unity of functional reality in the grand universe (106:1.4).
106:33: If God the Sevenfold functionally co-ordinates finite evolution, the Supreme Being synthesizes destiny attainment. The Supreme Being is the Deity culmination of grand universe evolution, signifying that the spirit nucleus will at last dominate the physical evolution around it (106:2.1). To understand Supremacy, we must distinguish three elements (106:2.2).
106:38: The spirit personality of God the Supreme on Havona
106:40: The experiential power gained and proved in time and space
106:42: Evolutionary power unified with and dominated by the spirit person
106:44: Because creatures, even mortals, take part personally in this tremendous undertaking, we gain the capacity to know the Supreme and to recognize ourselves as true children of this evolutionary Deity (106:2.5). Just as Michael shares the perfection of the Father, we too shall one day share the evolutionary perfection of the Supreme (106:2.6). Because God the Supreme is an experiential being, he can be completely experienced (106:2.7).
106:46: The absonite Architects make the plans, the Supreme Creators bring them into existence, and the Supreme Being completes their fullness (106:3.1). When the present age ends and almighty Supremacy appears, the first experiential Trinity, the Ultimate Trinity, will function fully (106:3.2).
106:55: Supreme Creators · Supreme Being · Architects of the Master Universe
106:58: God the Supreme · God the Ultimate · the Universe Consummator
106:61: The Paradise Trinity is an association of absolute Deities only, but creature personalities also contribute to the experiential Trinities. That there are Master Creator Sons among the Supreme Creators of the Ultimate Trinity means that genuine creature experience is included in it (106:3.3). Group associations can transcend individual abilities, and in the ages to come the Corps of the Finality will promulgate the purposes of the Deities as directed by the Ultimate Trinity (106:3.4).
106:63: The Ultimate Trinity co-ordinates the transcendental as transcendental, and in the eternal future it will further activate the presence of Ultimate Deity (106:4.1). God the Ultimate is the transcendental power-personalization that gives direction to the whole master universe, and the completed appearance of Ultimacy will signify the completion of the master creation (106:4.2).
106:64: Just as Supremacy is now present on Havona spiritually and personally, Ultimacy also exists there in an absonite and superpersonal sense (106:4.3). The transcendence of the finite can lead only to ultimate attainment; God the Ultimate transcends time and space but is still subabsolute (106:4.4).
106:66: When Supremacy and Ultimacy actually appear, the foundation is laid for the second experiential Trinity, the Absolute Trinity. This Trinity has the theoretical capacity to activate the three Absolutes of potentiality, but it will be fully formed only after the whole master universe is completed, out to the outermost space levels (106:5.1).
106:67: A Trinity is not in itself personal, but neither does it deny personality. Its members are not that Trinity as individuals; only together are they a Trinity (106:5.3). That is why the association of the three Absolutes of potentiality is not a Trinity, for only that which is deified can be a Trinity (106:5.4).
106:69: Trinities are always deity reality but never personality reality. (106:5.3)
106:72: The stage of the master universe seems sufficient for the actualization of the Supreme Being, the functioning of the Ultimate Trinity, the appearance of God the Ultimate, and the beginning of the Absolute Trinity. But the full functioning of the Absolute Trinity suggests something beyond the master universe (106:6.2). It is conjectured that in the cosmos-infinite beyond it, the Absolute Trinity may attain the absolute actualization of all potentials (106:6.3).
106:73: The eternal activity of the Absolute Trinity may experientialize the Absolutes of potentiality and personalize the Deity Absolute, so completing God the Absolute. God the Absolute is the third and last of the experiential Deities (106:6.5-6.6).
106:78: Finite — the culmination of evolutionary-experiential reality
106:80: Transcendental — the peak of transcendental reality
106:82: Absolute — the third and last experiential Deity
106:85: Quantitative infinity can never be fully realized. Within the three potential Absolutes there will always remain possibilities that no experiential development can exhaust (106:7.1). No being or universe can ever fully attain every aspect of final destiny (106:7.4).
106:86: But this is no cause for discouragement. We really do attain the Deity levels of the Sevenfold, Supremacy, and Ultimacy, and the infinity of God is the supreme assurance that possibilities of personality development and Deity association will remain throughout an endless future (106:7.6). Even when the master universe is completed, we will look back on its whole history as only a beginning, and the master universe will always be young (106:7.8).
106:88: ⟦Q 106:7.5⟧No matter how much of God you may attain, there will always remain much more of him, the existence of which you will not even suspect.⟦/Q⟧ (106:7.5)
106:91: The Trinity of Trinities is theoretically the sum of all experiential infinity, in which experiential infinity and existential infinity become one in the I AM (106:8.1). The presenter describes it as three levels of ever-enlarging unity (106:8.3-8.7).
106:96: The Paradise, Ultimate, and Absolute Trinities
106:98: The Supreme, the Ultimate, and the Absolute (the association of the experiential Deities)
106:100: The I AM — experienced as the Father-Infinite
106:102: In this association the Father-Son partnership passes through Son-Spirit, Spirit-Supreme, Supreme-Ultimate, and Ultimate-Absolute, and reaches Father-Infinite, completing the circle of reality (106:8.12). The second-level association has already appeared in our age in the deification of Majeston (106:8.20). And as personal creatures looking toward this distant possibility, we may infer that the final destiny of every personality is the final knowing of the Universal Father (106:8.22).
106:104: Experiential unification lies in the far future, but existential unification is already actual in the Paradise Trinity. Even at this moment, infinite reality is absolutely unified (106:9.1, 9.4). Time, space, and experience are our greatest helps in understanding relative reality, yet they are also the greatest barriers to a complete perception of reality (106:9.3).
106:106: Why we do not perceive the completed unity
106:111: Far removed from the absolute levels
106:113: Evolution through experience is the purpose of existence
106:115: In the Infinite there is no real change; apparent development comes from our growing capacity to receive (106:9.9). Every creature’s growth is proportional to its Father identification, and living the will of God is the eternal passport to infinity (106:9.11). Such a life is founded on truth, sensitive to beauty, and dominated by goodness; inwardly it glows with worship, and outwardly it shows itself in loving service (106:9.12).
106:117: Paper 106 unfolds the ladder of reality that begins with us, the incomplete finites, passes through Supremacy and Ultimacy, and reaches the absolute and infinity. God the Sevenfold helps our struggles now, the Supreme Being synthesizes that growth, and the experiential Trinities achieve ever greater unity in turn. The end can never be fully reached in all eternity, yet this is not frustration but the promise of endless growth. Infinite reality is already one in the Paradise Trinity, and as we live the will of God and grow more like the Father, we draw one step at a time toward that infinity.
